To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the provision of control power by power to heat plants is a viable alternative to base load power plant generation for the provision of control energy.

the use of electric power boilers in district heating systems could reduce system wide costs and emissions in the German power supply by up to 0.5 billion EUR/a (0.3 billion USD/a) and 2.3 million t CO2/a (2.5 million t CO2e/a) in 2025, respectively.
power to heat plants could be used as a cheap and flexible alternative for base load power plants to provide secondary control power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how power to heat systems can be used to provide negative control power.
the question whether power to heat plants could be a suitable instrument for the provision of control power.
the question of whether and under which conditions power to heat plants can contribute to the provision of negative secondary control power in Germany.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electric boilers in district heat grids can provide a cost effective solution for the provision of negative secondary control power in Germany.
power to heat systems can contribute to an efficient integration of fluctuating renewable energy sources in the power system and can reduce the overall costs of the power supply.

the integration of power to heat plants into the control power market is an economically efficient measure to reduce overall CO2 emission of the power supply in Germany and to enhance the integration of RES.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
power to heat plants are a promising technology for providing negative control power in the future German electricity market.
the use of electric heat pumps and electric boilers in district heat grids can be a promising option for the provision of secondary control power.
electric boilers in district heat grids could provide a cost efficient alternative to conventional base load power plants to provide control power in the German power system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electric boilers can contribute significantly to the cost effective integration of fluctuating renewable energy sources into the electricity system and thus help to reduce CO2 emissions.
power to heat plants could provide a cheap alternative for the provision of secondary control power and therefore could enhance the integration of RES.
power to heat plants can be a valuable instrument to reduce the overall system costs of the power supply by providing negative control power.
